What's so amazing about fur seals?

The fur seal, which moves between sea and land, is an amazing marine mammal that swims with its flipper feet and can also walk on land.

content.alt: Fur seal - Nature and science facts about fur seals
content.text:
Nature and science facts about fur seals

The fur seal is a pinniped marine mammal with flipper feet, and it can walk on land by bending its hind flippers forward (which sets it apart from the earless true seal). A thick layer of blubber (subcutaneous fat) keeps its body warm in the cold seawater, and it hunts by sensing the movement of fish with its long, sensitive whiskers. The pups grow up drinking their mother's milk, and they recognize and find their mother by her call.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the flipper feet (swimming and walking), the blubber (body warmth), the whiskers (sensing), and the mother and pup. It's great to talk together about, "How does the fur seal endure the cold sea?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Observe the fur seal swimming and walking at an aquarium or zoo. Explaining, "The thick fat keeps it warm just like a thick coat (that's blubber)," makes it easy to understand.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Can fur seals walk on land too?
A. Yes. They walk on land by bending their hind flippers forward. This is what sets them apart from the earless true seal.

Q. How do they endure the cold sea?
A. A thick layer of blubber (subcutaneous fat) keeps them warm. With their whiskers, they sense fish.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Watching them swim and walk at an aquarium or zoo, and talking about "blubber = a thick coat," both work well.
